programs.text: Start here Foundation Course 1: Introduction to the Soil Food Web Before compost, before teas, before microscopy, you must understand how the soil ecosystem actually functions. This course teaches the biological relationships that drive nutrient cycling, plant health, and long-term soil fertility. Learn more →

Start here Foundation Course 2: Biocomplete™ Compost Foundation Course 2 teaches you how to create biologically complete compost that rebuilds soil life. Learn proper materials, pile management, and application methods to support nutrient cycling, soil structure, and long-term plant health. Learn more →

Start here Foundation Course 3: BioComplete™ Liquid Amendments Foundation Course 3 teaches you how to prepare and apply biologically correct compost extracts and teas. Learn brewing principles, equipment use, and application strategies to deliver living microorganisms effectively and support soil health, plant Learn more →

Start here Foundation Course 4: Microscopy Microscopy teaches you how to use a compound microscope to identify and quantify soil microorganisms. Learn to assess bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and nematodes, interpret biological data, and make informed decisions to improve soil health. Learn more →

Hone your skills Soil Microscopy Seeing is believing, and when it comes to the regeneration of living soil, a microscope is your most powerful ally: Become a Soil Food Web Lab Tech, See what your soil really needs before spending time and money to improve it, Measure the real impact of your efforts near instantly, No more sending samples across the country for assessment | Complete on-site assessments yourself Learn more →

Hone your skills BioComplete™ Compost Production Learn to produce biologically complete compost that restores soil life, suppresses disease, and transforms what’s possible on your land. Discover how to redirect organic waste into a biologically rich amendment, grow the right microbes to support healthy soil and plants while minimizing the risk of human pathogens and weed seeds, and replace expensive, harmful chemical inputs with the power of biology and organic matter. Learn more →

Hone your skills Learn the Art and Science of Biological Liquid Amendments Build on your Soil Food Web Microscopy and BioComplete™ Compost Production skills by learning to purposefully breed, multiply, and extract key microbes for various real world field application needs Learn more →

Hone your skills Advanced Field Trial You've learned to see life in a microscope slide. You've built biologically complete compost from the ground up. You've brewed and applied biological liquid amendments. You understand, at a cellular level, what healthy soil looks like and why it matters. Now it's time to prove it in the field. Learn more →
Design systems Permaculture Design Certification Whole-system design: water, plants, structures, community, rooted in living soil. See the Permaculture Design Certification →

Understanding Ecosystem Health Introduction to Ecosystem Restoration : Module 1 Build a strong foundation in ecosystem restoration and learn how healthy ecosystems function. Explore the key factors that shape ecosystems, including soil, biodiversity, climate, water, and species interactions, while gaining the knowledge to recognize ecosystem degradation and support the restoration of healthy, resilient land. Learn more →

Ecological Processes & Ecosystem Restoration Introduction to Ecosystem Restoration : Module 2 Explore how species, ecological cycles, and natural processes work together to shape healthy ecosystems. Learn about invasive and keystone species, food webs, nutrient cycles, ecosystem services, ecological succession, marine ecosystems, and nature-based solutions for restoring and protecting our environment. Learn more →

Practical Ecosystem Restoration Introduction to Ecosystem Restoration : Module 3 Move from ecological theory into practical restoration principles. Explore ecosystem restoration strategies, site assessment, abiotic and biotic factors, aquatic impacts, population ecology, and real-world case studies to understand how damaged ecosystems can be assessed and restored. Learn more →

Practical Restoration & Recovery Introduction to Ecosystem Restoration : Module 4 Take ecosystem restoration from theory to practice. Learn about restoration standards, natural recovery, seed collection and propagation, planting strategies, species-level restoration, population ecology, and real-world restoration projects. Learn more →

This Is Where It All Began Mini Foundation Course Learn directly from the source with this Intro to the Foundations Mini Course. A 10-lesson mini course into the world of Living Soil and all the ways it can help regenerate the world's living systems. Walk away with a broad view of just how impactful this work can be when applied consistently by educated land stewards and practitioners. Learn more →

In person Workshops Build BioComplete™ Compost, create biological liquid amendments, and practice microscopy alongside Dr. Elaine's team of experienced mentors and an international community. See the calendar of workshops →

elaine_page: ← Back to Team Dr. Elaine Ingham Founder Dr. Elaine Ingham served as the Soil Food Web School’s Founder, Principal Ambassador, and Science and Research Advisor. Dr. Ingham began her college career at St. Olaf College, where she graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts. She earned her Master of Science in Marine Biology from Texas A&M and her Ph.D. in Soil Microbiology from Colorado State in 1981. From there, she completed her post-doc at the University of Georgia Institute of Ecology before serving as an Instructor and later an Associate Professor for many years at Oregon State University. During her travels, she served as the first President of the Soil Ecology Society, the Program Director for the Ecological Society of America, and a member of the American Society of Microbiology. In addition to starting Soil Foodweb Inc. 26 years ago, Dr. Ingham owned and then sold the Soil Foodweb Institute in Australia and served as Chief Scientist at the Rodale Institute. Dr. Ingham’s research is global, and her scientific papers date as far back as 1982, with research concerning ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence of arbuscular mycorrhizal root infections. Seventy-six papers later, she focused on milk comparison between organic and conventional farms in the United States. Dr. Ingham has written 6 book chapters for published books, participated in research teams publishing 17 technical reports, and has been a speaker at agricultural conferences in Great Britain, Brazil, Australia, and numerous states throughout America. Dr. Ingham served as the global leader in the Soil Food Web sciences and is highly respected worldwide for her achievements. In 2019, she teamed up with Luke Louka and created The Soil Food Web School (SFWS). Dr. Ingham passed in 2026, and the Soil Food Web Foundation exists to further her legacy.

page_text:/volunteer/: About the Foundation In service to the soil that sustains us all The Soil Food Web Foundation is a nonprofit organization carrying forward the life’s work of Dr. Elaine Ingham — empowering communities everywhere to restore and protect the Earth’s soil and living systems. Mission Our History What We Do Team Dr. Elaine’s Research Contact & Legal Our Mission To honor and grow Dr. Elaine Ingham’s legacy of empowering communities to restore and protect the Earth’s soil and living systems — by sharing teaching and learning about the soil food web, pursuing knowledge related to soil, plant, and planetary health, incubating regenerative agricultural and ecosystem practices, and building community and financial support for soil food web teaching, research, and practice. Our Vision Healthy, living soil in every terrestrial ecoregion on the planet — nurtured by local communities who understand why soil health is the foundation of ecosystem, agricultural, planetary, and human wellbeing. Our History Rooted in legacy, growing in impact What We Do Four ways we grow this work Teaching & Learning World-class education in soil biology, from foundation courses to professional certification, with workshops in a growing list of ecoregions and support that makes learning accessible. Pursuing Knowledge Replicating key experiments, opening our trial and case-study data, and advancing microscopy and lab methods — so more people understand why the soil food web works. Incubating Applied Practice Ecoregion hubs that integrate education, composting, microscopy, and consulting; partnerships with farmers to trial and document soil food web practices where they live. Building Community & Support A global network of students, volunteers, donors, and advisors who make this mission durable — and welcoming to newcomers. Dr. Elaine’s Research The woman who started it all Dr. Elaine Ingham pioneered research in soil biology across the final four decades of her life and made her science radically accessible — so that anyone, anywhere, could learn to restore the soil beneath their feet. This Foundation is her living legacy, and we hold it with care: not by asking the world to take her word for it, but by opening her science for the world to prove. Read her published research →
